## Requirements: WebSocket Runtime V2 architecture and integration

### Owner decision (2026-11-24)
Control messages, requests and real-time data are three independent dispatch domains sharing one physical WebSocket when suitable. Preserve #961/#1021 keyed ordering, #3439 Axum ingress, #3548 frame abstraction, #3547 generation-safe teardown, #4065 Relay half-open detection and #1645/#1925 terminal consistency. This is an evolutionary refactor, not a new protocol, broker, distributed workflow engine or forced three-socket topology.

### Baseline and work partition
Main e656d1f9c95baafc8735a2bb0274f668a2cc30d7; previous review baseline 6c10bfa34bbe29bd4874b8d2b2ceb4ce458f9324. 
- A (this issue): canonical architecture and final integrated proof; not an implementation gate for other packages.
- B: #4433 — bounded ingress, Control/Request dispatch, task supervision, process budgets and shared receive path.
- C: #4434 — classified outbound scheduler, writer and connection settlement.
- D: #4435 — Stream dispatch, flow control and business resource fences.
- E: #4436 — Knowledge ingest and semantic drift verification.
- F: #4437 — stability telemetry, baseline and diagnostic dashboards.

Owner decision: all six V2 issues are newly created. Historical issues are evidence and regression constraints only; do not reopen, reuse or depend on them for execution or acceptance. B/C/D/E/F have zero hard start dependencies on each other or on completion of A. A owns the final integrated proof and canonical architecture. Use existing adapter seams for independently testable PRs; reconcile the receive/write/stream integration at A, not by forcing all sibling work into one PR. Knowledge and telemetry begin at the current baseline and evolve with accepted deltas. Shared adapter file edits require scoped ownership and merge coordination, not issue-wide serialization.

### Contract
- One reader and writer per physical connection; common transport-neutral Runtime owns decode/validation/admission, task supervision, lifecycle and queue mechanics. Host owns authentication/authorization and domain handlers. Server, Agent P2P, Agent central and Relay adapters share mechanisms, not necessarily policy values.
- Dispatch class is provider-owned metadata derived alongside the existing route declarations, not untrusted peer priority, wire prefix guessing, or a second ProtocolDescriptor registry. Protocol categories Operation/Notification/Control are orthogonal. RPC responses correlate by validated identity/id/generation ahead of ordinary dispatch; auth/register and mode transitions fence dependent work.
- Control: bounded reserved admission; fast completion resolution; no slow business await in reader. Request: bounded concurrent/keyed/task execution, overload explicit before admission, accepted operations receive outcome or connection-loss semantics; no blind replay of side effects. Stream: reliable ordered input, recoverable sequenced output, latest-state coalescence; provider owns cursor/generation/credit/authority and barriers between stream and mutations.
- Count and byte limits per connection and process, including retained task records, pending requests, active connections and oversized frames; enforce atomic/nonblocking admission or deterministic rollback. Outbound priority is fair and bounded; socket writes have finite deadline, physical TCP HOL is acknowledged.
- Stable interface boundary: dispatcher takes validated envelope + host route policy; execution handles admission/owned work; writer consumes classified frames; stream provider owns stream contract; all emit the telemetry semantics owned by #4437, preserving relevant historical #975 naming conventions without requiring that issue. Do not require a shared giant PR: packages can develop and merge their own components behind existing adapters; only integrated proof awaits all owners. No unapproved wire changes; if observable error semantics change, follow protocol version policy.
- Baseline before fixing production SLO. Mixed-load regression uses isolated CI Server/Agent/private tmux, configured low budgets, gated slow handlers and deterministic fault injection. No production load probe.

### Success Criteria
- [x] SC-01 Canonical architecture at docs/architecture/websocket-runtime.md defines Control/Request/Stream independently from Protocol Kernel wire categories, single Reader/Writer, one resource owner, explicit overload and lifecycle invariants; cross-links protocol.md and records current vs target behavior.
- [x] SC-02 An exact-source route inventory covers Server, Agent P2P, Agent central, Relay and Web adapter boundaries; every served wire is classified by its provider-owned semantic policy or explicitly refused, without a second consumer-visible contract registry.
- [ ] SC-03 On integrated staging, a source-aligned mixed-load protocol/runtime Case proves simultaneous control completion, independent requests and terminal streaming under bounded saturation; no silent loss, stale-generation mutation, ordering violation or unbounded task growth; disconnect settles connection-owned work.

SC mapping: SC-01 SCN-08 (exact document and links); SC-02 SCN-01 (source and protocol-integrity/codegen plus route coverage negative fixture); SC-03 SCN-03 (approved full-stack-local protocol/runtime Case at staging, barrier-controlled slow handler + terminal input/output + heartbeat + reconnect; assert frames, queue/worker counters and teardown). No blanket Full E2E on children.

## Acceptance Plan
```yaml
acceptance:
  SC-01:
    when: pr
    method: agent
  SC-02:
    when: pr
    method: agent
  SC-03:
    when: merged
    branch: staging
    method: case
```

| SC-02 | Pass | run 45319720363; ref 58a61368f4b43e77cefbcef5259ee4f8d7c03fbd; source agent-qwen; inventory: exact-source route inventory covers all five boundaries; policy: every served wire classified by provider-owned semantic policy; validation: explicit refusal of unknown wires specified; gate: websocket-route-inventory gate provides automated verification; summary: Complete route inventory with semantic classification and gate verification |
| SC-03 | Pending | - |

## E2E Verification
### New
- none: source-aligned protocol/runtime Case rather than a new browser interaction

- terminal-consistency-faults
- terminal-io
- terminal-attach-bootstrap
